messages:
support-lead: customer report incoming — multiple customers hitting 502/504s on /v1/generate since the 10:00 canary roll. High error rate and timeouts. forwarding logs and customer ids.
ops-oncall-bot: alert: API 5xx spike detected on hosted-inference (canary=canary-2026-03-17-10). spike starts +2m after canary rollout. :rotating_light:
jordan: copying raw metrics — seeing gateway 502s and some 504 request timeouts. 95th latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.2s. any recent config flags toggled in this canary?
sarah: yes — canary toggled `ENABLE_CONTIGUOUS_PREFETCH` and a namespace-level env `BATCH_WINDOW_MS` got set to `0` as part of the batching perf experiment. not supposed to be 0, should default to 5.
lee: ah that aligns with the error patterns — KV cache eviction thrash when prefetch runs with zero window, we saw backend pools saturate and gRPC backpressure -> gateway 502.
support-lead: customers are impacted. we need immediate mitigation and rollback plan. can we reduce canary traffic weight and toggle flag off?
mina: I can scale down the canary weight via router policy. running: `curl -X POST https://orch.internal/rollout/adjust -d '{"canary":"canary-2026-03-17-10","weight":5}'` — holding at 5% now.
jordan: good. also please flip `ENABLE_CONTIGUOUS_PREFETCH` to false in the canary env. patch applied?
sarah: applying patch, patch diff: ```yaml
- name: ENABLE_CONTIGUOUS_PREFETCH
  value: "true"
+ name: ENABLE_CONTIGUOUS_PREFETCH
+ value: "false"
- name: BATCH_WINDOW_MS
- value: "0"
+ name: BATCH_WINDOW_MS
+ value: "5"
```
ops-oncall-bot: deploy-bot reports: canary-2026-03-17-10 config update succeeded, rollout weight 5%. health checks still flapping but error rate dropped ~60% in last minute. :eyes:
lee: still seeing a tail of 502s from older client connections hitting old canary instances — recommend drain connections on canary hosts and evict unhealthy pods. `kubectl rollout restart` might not be enough; perform graceful drain + force terminate on the canary nodes.
support-lead: coordinate with customers: posting a status update on status.redwood.ai with ETA 30m.
jordan: to be safe, prepare full rollback manifest (previous image tag `release-2026-03-16-22`) and hold until we confirm stable. if errors continue after flag flip, execute rollback.
sarah: creating rollback PR now and tagging infra. PR link: https://git.redwood.ai/repo/infra/rollouts/pull/432 — includes env revert and health probe bump.
deploy-bot: action: started rollback job for canary-2026-03-17-10 -> target image release-2026-03-16-22 (dry-run checks passed).
mina: customer metrics showing latency back to baseline for most tenants. still monitoring.
lee: ops checklist: 1) drain canary nodes 2) evict pods with stale KV caches 3) increase readiness probe timeout from 2s -> 8s in rollback PR 4) remove `BATCH_WINDOW_MS=0` from any remaining env overrides.
jordan: support, please collect one full request trace and the backend pod logs for the 502 stack (include `grpc-status` and `upstream-time`). attach to the incident ticket.
support-lead: on it. pulling traces and will DM customers with explanation + reopening support tickets if needed.
ops-oncall-bot: error rate back under threshold, closing incident alert. keeping incident open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
sarah: postmortem notes starter: root cause = misconfigured experiment env var (`BATCH_WINDOW_MS=0`) combined with contiguous prefetch enabled, caused cache eviction and backend saturation during canary traffic spike. remediation = rollback + stronger validation on env types (reject `0` for window), add canary automation guard to disallow env-level zero values in rollout.
mina: adding runbook step to require a quick smoke test that hits KV-cache-heavy routes before increasing canary weight above 10%.
support-lead: thanks team — will file follow-up ticket for guard rails and customer communications. closing thread for now.
